The Leadership Model That Finally Made Sense of How I Actually Work

Leadership models are useful when they help explain what you do under pressure, not just what you value in theory.

Pupsi Phull · Phull Insights22 September 20262 min readLeadership & Transformation
Evidence boundary

Personal analysis and professional reflection based on earlier postgraduate work. Named-company examples describe historical research, not current 2026 corporate policies, figures or commitments. No unpublished case result is represented as a verified outcome.

Why this matters

Operational leaders have to make decisions across competing needs: customers, colleagues, performance, risk and long-term capability.

What the evidence suggests

This reflection draws on postgraduate leadership study and professional experience. The most useful lens was not a single ideal style, but a disciplined way to notice how personal values affect decisions and relationships.

What it looks like in practice

Responsible leadership becomes visible in ordinary choices: who is consulted, what evidence is challenged, what trade-off is explained, and whether a decision can be revisited when its effects become clear.

Practical next steps

Three things leaders can do now

01

Name the stakeholders who bear the cost of a decision.

02

Ask where your preferred solution may conflict with your stated values.

03

Create a review point to test the effect after implementation.

Phull Insights Perspective

The view beneath the headline.

A leadership model should increase accountability, not offer a flattering label. Its value lies in improving the next difficult decision.
